h: Make a South Downs day of it
p: Amberley Museum is one of the easiest attractions in Sussex to fold into a bigger day out, thanks to its spot right next to the station and the South Downs Way. Walkers often combine a few hours at the museum with a stretch of the trail, which crosses the River Arun close by and climbs up on to the downs for big views across the Weald. Even a short walk up the hill gives you a cracking panorama over the valley.

Amberley village is worth a wander in its own right, with thatched cottages, flint walls and a historic castle that's now a hotel. Below the village, Amberley Wild Brooks is a stretch of wet grazing marsh that's lovely for birdwatching, especially in winter when the water levels rise and waterfowl move in.

A few miles down the river, Arundel is a must if you've got time. The castle towers over the little town, and there are independent shops, tearooms and riverside walks, plus the WWT wetland centre on the edge of town. Bignor Roman Villa, with its famous mosaic floors, is a short drive in the other direction for anyone who fancies going even further back in time.

At the museum, keep an eye on the timetable for the day. Buses and trains don't run all the time, and event days, such as transport rallies and craft fairs, can be some of the most fun to visit. Comfy shoes are essential, as the site is spread out across the old pit, and the paths include a few slopes.
